d3/d3.summary: A free, open-source JavaScript library for creating dynamic, data-driven visualizations using a low-level, web-standards-based approach.
patterns: Low-level, standards-based rendering (HTML/CSS/SVG) for maximum flexibility
Modular, foundational design intended to be extended by higher-level chart libraries
Direct DOM manipulation paradigm enabling custom graphic authoring
Modular source organization in src/ with parallel test coverage in test/
Documentation-centric layout using docs/ and img/ for static content and visual examples
Interactive documentation powered by .vue components alongside .md and .js files
Configuration and metadata managed via .json files typical of modern JS toolchains
Theme extension via base theme inheritance
Dynamic module execution via Observable Runtime
Graceful error handling with environment-aware fallbacks
best_practices: Fetch external data at build time to optimize runtime performance
Extend official base themes rather than implementing from scratch
Use try/catch with CI environment checks to prevent local build failures
Separate configuration, theme logic, and data fetching into distinct modules
Leverage TypeScript for type-safe documentation tooling
insights: D3 has sustained significant adoption and community growth for over a decade
Its architecture prioritizes granular control and flexibility over out-of-the-box chart templates
It serves as a critical infrastructure layer powering many modern data visualization tools
The project maintains a robust ecosystem with dedicated documentation, examples, and community support channels
The mix of .vue, .js, and .md strongly indicates an interactive documentation site where code examples are rendered live for users.
The explicit separation of src/ and test/ reflects a mature, test-driven development workflow essential for a widely-used data visualization library.
The structure suggests a build pipeline that bundles modular JavaScript into distributable formats while maintaining a rich, component-driven docs experience.
The documentation leverages VitePress's data plugin system for static site generation efficiency
Interactive D3 examples are embedded directly using Observable's runtime, enhancing developer experience
Environment-aware API fetching indicates a mature CI/CD pipeline strategy for documentation builds
Modular theme architecture supports easy customization and maintenance
d3/d3.readme_insights: Standard open-source library layout with clear separation between source code, tests, documentation, and assets. The project uses JavaScript as the core implementation language, supplemented by Markdown for static docs, Vue components for interactive examples, JSON for configuration, and PNG for visual assets.

It helps you find vulnerabilities in your applications, APIs, networks, DNS, and cloud config
